key_insight: 4DCodeBench tests whether AI agents can reconstruct dynamic scenes by generating executable graphics code that captures motion, deformation, fluid flow, and fracture.
engineering_relevance: The benchmark is relevant to solid mechanics because it probes whether models can infer physically meaningful structure and time-evolving behavior from video, which is central to inverse modeling of deformable and damage-prone systems.
method: Curates real-world videos and synthetic dynamic scenes.
Requires agents to output executable graphics programs rather than fixed descriptions.
Evaluates reconstruction across diverse physical phenomena including deformation, fluid flow, and fracture.
evidence_signal: The authors benchmark frontier models on curated video scenes and report that strong static reconstruction performance does not reliably carry over to complex dynamics.
watch_item: Reconstruction quality may depend heavily on the benchmark’s scene design and the gap between synthetic and real-world dynamics, so results may not directly transfer to engineering applications.
paper_title: 4DCodeBench: Benchmarking Agents on Inverse Graphics of Dynamic Scenes
